correctness.rationale: The scalar stationarity equation for the unique real p-mean, sum_i sign(m−x_i)|m−x_i|^(p−1)=0, gives coordinate monotonicity, translation covariance and |m(x)−m(y)|<=||x−y||_infinity. It yields global n^(1/p) and the n=2 midpoint identity. For n>=3, p<2, an input with one zero residual and balancing remaining residuals gives m(x+epsilon e_i)/epsilon→1; for p>2, differentiating off the diagonal yields nonnegative weights w_i proportional |r_i|^(p−2), with each w_i<=1/2 by residual balance and concavity. Hölder then gives exact (n/2)^(1/p), reached as a derivative at (1,-1,0,...). Continuity/segment split handles the singular diagonal; p=2 is the orthogonal average, n=2 is the midpoint. Proof is correct across all claimed ranges.
